newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian data firm signs $2.75m investment deal.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian data firm signs $2.75m investment deal.

text.p: A Tanzanian data firm has signed a $2.75 million investment deal to help finance a $10 million data communications project, a company statement said.

Privately-run Datel Tanzania Ltd, in which the state-run telecommunications corporation is a major shareholder, said it was developing a domestic and international data network service as part of an ongoing modernisation of the country's outdated communications sector.
The investment agreement was signed in Paris on June 30 between Datel and the International Finance Corporation, a member of the World Bank Group, the statement said.
The IFC investment comprises a loan of $2.25 million plus $507,500 in equity subscription.

"The funds thus injected are to enable Datel to establish a network for the fast and efficient data transfer both within Tanzania and internationally. The network and services are to be extended to the rural areas," said the statement.

Datel, which began operations in 1996, lists its shareholders as Nexus International (36 percent), state-run Tanzania Telecommunications Ltd (35 percent), IFC (14.5 percent) and Proparco of France (14.5 percent).

Company customers listed include several major organisations in Tanzania including the central Bank of Tanzania (BoT), Tanzania Cigarette Company (TCC), Total Oil, Tritel (operators of a digital mobile phone network), Furaha Finance and Internet service providers.

Datel said it expects to sign up additional customers in the near future, including Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA), Tanzania Railways Corporation, Tanzania National Parks and the Civil Aviation Authority.
